Some experts note that cloth masks mainly protect others rather than the wearer, reinforcing the idea of source control—capturing droplets at their source to protect the community [2]. Modeling and policy guidance suggest that widespread mask use can significantly curb transmission, with advisory bodies encouraging high population-level adherence as part of broader pandemic control strategies, [0, 7]. If you choose to wear a non-medical mask, continue proven precautions such as keeping distance and washing hands frequently, since masks work best as one layer in a comprehensive prevention approach rather than as a standalone measure,, [3, 4, 5].
